Lessons.Title: Absolute Value Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goals: express numerical distances and contextual tolerances with |x−a|, construct transformed absolute-value graphs, solve absolute equations and graph absolute inequalities.
The absolute value |x−a| is a nonnegative distance. For a nonnegative tolerance d, |x−a|≤d includes all x from a−d through a+d, while |x−a|≥d describes two external rays.
The graph f(x)=a|x−h|+k has vertex (h,k). If a>0 it opens upward and attains minimum k; if a<0 it opens downward and attains maximum k.
For |A|=c: if c>0 solve A=±c; if c=0 solve A=0; if c<0 there are no real solutions. Check each candidate in the original formula.
A strict inside inequality |A|<c has two simultaneous bounds; an outside inequality |A|>c describes separate rays. When multiplying or dividing inequalities by a negative factor, reverse the sign.
Graph intercepts require setting the appropriate coordinate to zero. Always state endpoints and included/excluded bounds for real-domain and graph window problems.
Independent Edulytics Cool-down: (a) Solve |x+2|≤4 using interval notation. (b) For f(x)=−2|x−3|+4 state vertex, range and x-intercepts. (c) Explain why |3x−1|=−2 has no solution.
Independent Try It 1 — Distance from center. Find all x within two units of −1.
Independent Try It 2 — Test passing score. A score within 15 points of 75 meets a stated requirement. Express inclusive absolute-value inequality.
Independent Try It 3 — Graph a V transformation. Reflect f(x)=|x| over x-axis, then shift right 2 and up 4.
Independent Try It 4 — Solve for both roots. Find zeros of f(x)=|2x+3|−5.
Independent Try It 5 — Locate graph intercepts. Find intercepts of f(x)=−|x+1|+4.
Independent Try It 6 — Inclusive absolute inequality. Solve |x−3|≤5.
Independent Try It 7 — Inequality after dividing by negative. Solve −2|k−4|≤−6.

KeyConcepts.Title: Absolute distance
KeyConcepts.Definition: |x−a| denotes nonnegative real distance of x from a.
KeyConcepts.Rule: |x−a|≤d for d≥0 is the closed interval [a−d,a+d].

KeyConcepts.Title: Absolute V-shape
KeyConcepts.Rule: Sign of a controls opening, |a| controls steepness; domain all real.

KeyConcepts.Title: Absolute equations
KeyConcepts.Definition: If |A|=c with c>0, then A=c or A=−c.
KeyConcepts.Rule: For c<0 there are no solutions; for c=0 solve A=0.

KeyConcepts.Title: Absolute inequalities
KeyConcepts.Definition: Inside ≤ yields intersection; outside ≥ yields two rays for a nonnegative bound.
KeyConcepts.Rule: For negative bounds examine the nonnegative absolute value before case splitting.

KeyConcepts.Title: Intercepts
KeyConcepts.Definition: Set y=0 for x-intercepts and x=0 for y-intercept.
KeyConcepts.Rule: An upward shifted V may have no x-intercepts even though it always has a y-intercept.

KeyConcepts.Title: Context and units
KeyConcepts.Rule: State center, allowable distance, inclusion, units and interpretation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Viewing windows
KeyConcepts.Definition: A bounded plotted x-window generally has a range different from the full real-domain range.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check vertex inside the window and both included endpoints.

SummaryPoints: Absolute value represents nonnegative distance from a target.
V-shaped functions have a vertex determined by horizontal and vertical shifts.
An equation |A|=c has no real solution if c<0.
Inside inequalities produce bounded intervals; outside inequalities usually produce two rays.
Always check boundary inclusions, intercepts, graph window and physical units.
Teacher reviews diagrams and source-skill reasoning in Stage C.

CommonMistakes.Correction: Conclude no real solutions before splitting.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Inside a radius imposes simultaneous lower and upper bounds.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Neglecting to reverse inequality when dividing by a negative multiplier.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: This reverses which real values satisfy the inequality.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Reverse the comparison direction on negative division.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Confusing the vertex location with graph intercepts.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Vertex generally has nonzero x or y coordinate.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Set x=0/y=0 explicitly to find intercepts.
